newsitem.title: UK: Malt exporters eye higher EU refund on Thursday.
newsitem.headline: Malt exporters eye higher EU refund on Thursday.

text.p: Europe's maltsters are hoping that the European Union's (EU) Commission will bow to market forces and set a higher export refund in its weekly cereals review on Thursday.

The current refund of 32.50 Ecus per tonne attracted little demand, igniting a row between exporters and the Commission over what maltsters said was a subsidy which failed to give them a level playing field on the world market.
That refund, set on September 12, may be subject to review this week according to a monthly review system now in place.
"Malt exporters are watching the market very carefully for what the Commision will do this week," said one maltster.

"We're still not impatiently banging on the door because the market hasn't settled properly, but it would be very nice to see a consideration take place this week," he added. The malt refund is usually linked to the most recent two barley refunds and has a validity of nearly a year. But malsters said the Commission has waived this practice last month.

Slow demand was partly blamed for ultra-thin interest in the current restitution, but a stronger reason was a belief among exporters that the Commission would have to raise the refund if it wants to cover a hefty barley sale to Saudi Arabia.

"When that refund was set the market was still resolving itself round barley availability around the world. But we feel that once this comes to a resolution the Commission will be able see their way clear to producing a more equitable refund," said one malsters' representative.

Exporters, backed by Britain and Belgium, argue that malt should be set at 30 percent above the prevailing barley export refund. This implies a refund of 40.27 Ecus based on last week's barley allotment. The Saudi barley sale at an average $135 per tonne meanwhile implies a malt refund of 35 Ecus.
